literal: " At the time evaluating hall and precinct performance, He's government was top grade; robes, horses, and objects were bestowed and proclaimed throughout the realm.
idiomatic: In the performance review He's province ranked first; rewards were proclaimed empire-wide.

literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He was later summoned as grand commandant.

literal: The Rouran raided the frontier; He followed the imperial carriage and defeated them.
idiomatic: When the Rouran raided, He campaigned with the emperor and routed them.

literal: When Xianwen was about to transmit the throne to Zituo, Prince of Jingzhao, at the time He was area commander of all armies garrisoned south of the desert; he then sent a rapid dispatch summoning He.
idiomatic: As Xianwen prepared to abdicate to the Prince of Jingzhao, He was summoned from the desert garrison.

literal: When He arrived he sternly and firmly held that it could not be.
idiomatic: He arrived and flatly refused the abdication.

literal: Immediately an edict ordered him to bear the staff and present the imperial seal and cord to Xiaowen.
idiomatic: An edict then had him present the imperial seal to Xiaowen.

literal: That year Hexi rebelled; an edict sent He to campaign; many submitted and were defeated.
idiomatic: When Hexi rebelled that year, He subdued many by force and surrender.

literal: He according to ancient and modern military methods and the sayings of former Confucians and elders, briefly selecting the most essential, made twelve formation diagrams and presented them; Xianwen looked and praised them.
idiomatic: He distilled ancient tactics into twelve battle diagrams that Xianwen praised.

literal: He again was area commander of the armies of the three routes garrisoned south of the desert.
idiomatic: He again commanded the three-route army south of the desert.

literal: At the time each year autumn and winter the army was sent out in three routes together to prepare against northern raiders; by mid-spring they then withdrew.
idiomatic: Each autumn three columns marched north; by spring they withdrew.

literal: He because it wearied the capital and was also not a long plan for defending the frontier, then submitted, asking to recruit from the garrisons of the provinces thirty thousand men with martial courage, restore their corvée and taxes, richly add relief and support, and divide them into three parts.
idiomatic: He argued the yearly expeditions exhausted the capital and proposed recruiting thirty thousand frontier warriors with tax relief in three divisions.

literal: Between two garrisons build a fort; in each fort place ten thousand men, supply twelve strong crossbows per bed, three hundred martial guard chariots.
idiomatic: Between two posts he would build forts of ten thousand men with heavy crossbows and war chariots.

literal: Each crossbow bed was supplied six oxen; each martial guard chariot was supplied two oxen.
idiomatic: Each crossbow team took six oxen; each chariot two.

literal: Make many cavalry lances and all instruments; appoint two generals of martial strategy to pacify and reassure them.
idiomatic: He would stock lances and gear and station two generals to command them.

literal: In winter then drill arms; in spring then plant—both garrison and both cultivate—then the army would not be weary and there would be surplus stores.
idiomatic: Winter drill, spring farming—troops would stay fed without annual marches from the capital.

literal: Also south of the White Road at three places establish granaries; transport rent grain from nearby provinces and garrisons to fill them.
idiomatic: He would build three granaries south of the White Road filled with nearby rents.

literal: Full food and full troops to prepare against the unforeseen—in affairs it was convenient.
idiomatic: Full granaries and full ranks would guard the frontier cheaply.

literal: One must not every year always raise the masses.
idiomatic: The realm need not mobilize every year.

literal: The affair was shelved without reply.
idiomatic: The throne filed it without answer.

literal: He memorialized claiming illness begging for his bones; up to three times; then it was permitted.
idiomatic: He begged retirement on illness three times before it was granted.

literal: When the court had great deliberations all came to inquire of him; he was also given robes, medicine, and delicacies.
idiomatic: Great debates still sought him out; the court sent robes, medicine, and delicacies.

literal: In the second month of the first year of Taihe he treated illness at the hot springs.
idiomatic: In Taihe year one, second month, he took the hot springs for his health.

literal: Xiaowen and the Empress Dowager Wenming repeatedly sent envoys to ask after news; the imperial physician attended the illness.
idiomatic: Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming sent physicians and repeated inquiries.

literal: The illness was grave; he returned to the capital.
idiomatic: When he grew worse he returned to the capital.

literal: He then left instructions to his sons, saying: "I recently because of old illness declined affairs, not aware that Heaven's kindness lowered grace, rank reaching you.
idiomatic: Dying, he told his sons, "I quit office with age, never expecting ennoblement to reach you."

literal: You must not be arrogant and stingy, not be dissolute and negligent, not be extravagant and overstepping, not be jealous.
idiomatic: Be neither arrogant nor stingy, neither slack nor jealous.

literal: In doubt think to ask; in speech think to examine; in conduct think to be respectful; in dress think to measure.
idiomatic: Question what you doubt; weigh your words; honor your conduct; measure your dress.

literal: Restrain evil and display good; be close to the worthy and far from flatterers; what the eye sees must be true, what the ear attends must be upright; be loyal and diligent in serving the ruler, pure and sparing in facing yourself.
idiomatic: Repress evil, uplift good, trust the worthy, shun flatterers, see clearly, hear straight, serve loyally, live sparely.

literal: After my end, for burial, timely dress in a single coffin is enough to express filial heart; bright spirit bright vessels—none are to be used.
idiomatic: Bury me in plain timely dress in one coffin; no bright spirit goods at all.

literal: " In the third year he died; posthumously awarded Palace Attendant, Grand Commandant, seal and cord of Prince of Longxi; posthumous title Prince Xuan.
idiomatic: In year three he died, posthumously palace attendant, grand commandant, and Prince Xuan of Longxi.

literal: He was given the towering carriage and command robes, warm bright secret vessels, and buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He was buried at Jinling with imperial funeral gear.

literal: The eldest son Yan, nature careful and thick, in youth loved learning, held the post of Palace Attendant Within the Hall, was enfeoffed Viscount of Guangwu.
idiomatic: Eldest son Yan was dutiful and studious, palace attendant within the hall, viscount of Guangwu.

literal: He died; posthumously awarded Governor of Liangzhou, Marquis of Guangwu, posthumous title Jian.
idiomatic: He died, posthumously governor of Liangzhou, marquis of Guangwu, posthumous name Jian.

literal: His son Lin inherited.
idiomatic: His son Lin inherited.

literal: Yan's younger brother Sil, later given the name Huai, was modest, respectful, broad, and elegant and had great measure.
idiomatic: Yan's brother Sil, later Huai, was modest, spacious, and magnanimous.

literal: At the end of Wencheng he was Palace Attendant Within the Hall.
idiomatic: At the end of Wencheng he was palace attendant within the hall.

literal: His father He declined old age; an edict ordered him to receive his father's rank.
idiomatic: When He retired, an edict let Huai inherit his father's rank.

literal: Later bearing the staff he was area commander of all armies garrisoned south of the desert; the Rouran greatly feared him.
idiomatic: Commanding south of the desert, he made the Rouran fear him.

literal: On return he was removed as Director Within the Hall and went out as Garrison Commander of Chang'an and Governor of Yongzhou.
idiomatic: Returning, he directed the masters of writing within the hall, then governed Yong from Chang'an.

literal: Pure, sparing, with benevolent government, skilled at comforting and cherishing; banditry ceased.
idiomatic: Frugal and kind, he soothed the people until banditry stopped.

literal: He was again appointed Director Within the Hall, added Palace Attendant, and participated in affairs of All Offices.
idiomatic: He was again director within the hall, palace attendant, and joined all-office affairs.

literal: He again was area commander of all armies campaigning against the Rouran; six-route grand generals all received his command.
idiomatic: Campaigning against the Rouran again, six grand generals answered to him.

literal: He was transferred to Master of Writing and participated in deliberating codes and statutes.
idiomatic: He became master of writing and helped revise the law.

literal: Later he was then lowered to duke.
idiomatic: He was later reduced to duke.

literal: He was removed as Governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: He was made governor of Sizhou.

literal: He again followed the imperial carriage on southern campaign and was added General of the Guards and led central military affairs.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign he was made guards general in charge of central armies.

literal: He left office on his mother's mourning; silk three hundred bolts and grain one thousand piculs were bestowed.
idiomatic: For his mother's mourning he received three hundred bolts of silk and a thousand piculs of grain.

literal: The imperial carriage visited Dai; an edict ordered envoys to mourn and comfort.
idiomatic: When the emperor went to Dai, envoys were sent to condole.

literal: In the second year of Jingming he was removed as Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing on the Left and added Special Advancement.
idiomatic: In Jingming year two he became left vice minister with special advancement.

literal: At the time an edict because corrupt officials committing crimes often fled and hid, when the general amnesty was issued they were all released alike.
idiomatic: An edict said corrupt officials who fled would be amnestied like all others.

literal: From now on for crimes, not asking light or heavy, those who hide and flee shall all be banished far.
idiomatic: Henceforth all fugitives, whatever the crime, would be exiled.

literal: If they forever avoid and do not emerge, brothers shall be moved in their place.
idiomatic: If they never surfaced, their brothers would serve the sentence.

literal: Huai then memorialized: "Respectfully examining the regulations, fugitive officials are not within the scope of pardon."
idiomatic: Huai replied that fugitive officials were never within amnesty by regulation.

literal: I reflect that the sage court's grace differs from former pardons; all those banished on the road still receive return; how much more those not yet sent out yet still dispatched to frontier garrison?
idiomatic: Exiles already on the road were being recalled—how could fresh fugitives be sent to the frontier?

literal: Examining prefects and magistrates committing crimes, fugitives are many; salary and bounty being superior, they still have such lapses; when they receive gracious pardon they suddenly can return.
idiomatic: Many magistrates fled despite rich salaries, yet would return under grace.

literal: Now alone to afflict this class—I fear it is not a uniform law.
idiomatic: Punishing only the lowborn, he argued, was not uniform law.

literal: " The memorial was submitted; the Gate and Chamber because the established form had been promulgated, rejected the memorial and did not allow it.
idiomatic: The memorial reached the gate; the edict stood and was rejected.

literal: Huai again memorialized: "Your servant thinks law values passing through, government values simplicity; the setting of penal statutes is to net wrongdoers—if reason is provided for, it is not in a prolix code."
idiomatic: Huai wrote again: law should be simple; nets need not be tangled.

literal: Bowing and seeking the regulations, below merit rank, crimes arising and flight, meeting grace are not pardoned.
idiomatic: Below merit rank, fleeing criminals were denied amnesty.

literal: Though wishing to cut off the wicked path, it is not a passing form.
idiomatic: That rule stifled crime but was no universal pattern.

literal: Respectfully examining the matter regulations—infringing on office and ruining law, solely occupying beyond the current—are all above the ninth rank men all pure and white?
idiomatic: Did only men below the ninth rank sin, while every higher officer was spotless?

literal: The various prefectural governors and magistrates, offices in the pure current, even to greed and defilement, affairs arising and flight and concealment, yet meeting grace are excused from crime;
idiomatic: High prefects who fled corruption were pardoned while merit-rank men alone were hunted;

literal: below merit rank alone they seek this precedent.
idiomatic: only the humble were denied the same mercy.

literal: Like this, then leniency is spread on the upper stream while law is sharp on the lower; nurturing things has difference; grace and punishment are not equal.
idiomatic: Thus the mighty were indulged and the low crushed—unequal mercy.

literal: Moreover treason floods heaven; passing grace still spares; officials committing slight crimes alone do not receive pardon—making the great pardon's canon not pass, the road of giving life blocked;
idiomatic: Treason itself could be pardoned, yet petty official crimes could not—choking the amnesty itself;

literal: advancing it violates ancient canon, retreating it opposes present statutes.
idiomatic: It offended both antiquity and the current code.

literal: Your servant in youth trod the heavenly offices; in old age bore the pivot's weight; whenever I saw lawsuits, coming and going I sighed in bitterness; I then led my foolish view and thought it should stop.
idiomatic: Long in office, he had watched suits break men and urged the policy be dropped.

literal: " The memorial was submitted; Emperor Xuanwu accepted it.
idiomatic: Xuanwu accepted the memorial.

literal: That year he was removed as Grand General of Cavalry and Grand Rectifier of Liangzhou.
idiomatic: That year he became grand general of cavalry and grand rectifier of Liangzhou.

literal: Huai again memorialized: "In the past when Shizu ascended to the far journey, Nan'an held the throne; going out to pay homage at the eastern temple he was murdered by the traitor minister Zong Ai."
idiomatic: Huai recalled how Emperor Shizu died, Nan'an reigned, and Zong Ai murdered him at the eastern temple.

literal: At the time Emperor Gaozong avoided calamity, dragon hidden in the park; Zong Ai had a different plot; the divine throne was not yet established.
idiomatic: Gaozong hid in the park while Zong Ai plotted and the throne stood empty.

literal: Your servant's late father He with Zhangsun Kehou, Lu Li, and others welcomed Gaozong and succeeded to the august precious mandate.
idiomatic: His father He with Zhangsun Kehou and Lu Li enthroned Gaozong.

literal: Li because of supporting and bearing the sacred person, personally witnessed, received appointment as General Who Pacifies the Army, Duke of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: Li, who carried the emperor in his arms, became general who pacifies the army, master of writing duke, prince of Pingyuan.

literal: In the second year of Xing'an, pursuing discussion of merit in fixing the plan, your servant's late father's rank was advanced to Prince of Xiping.
idiomatic: In Xing'an year two his father was raised to Prince of Xiping for enthroning the emperor.

literal: In the last year of Huangxing, Emperor Xianzu was about to transmit the great throne to the Prince of Jingzhao; your servant's late father at the time was area commander of all generals garrisoned at Wuchuan, was summoned to the capital, and specially received consultation.
idiomatic: When Xianzu would abdicate to Jingzhao, his father was summoned from Wuchuan for counsel.

literal: Your servant's late father firmly held it could not be; Xianzu after long time then permitted it; he then ordered your servant's late father to bear the staff and present the imperial seal and cord to Gaozu.
idiomatic: His father refused the abdication until Xianzu yielded, then handed Gaozu the seal.

literal: By the sixteenth year of Taihe, Li's son Rui reported to the secretariat, saying his dead father with your servant's late father supported and established Gaozong; the court pursued the record and enfeoffed Rui Duke of Julu commandery, state-founder.
idiomatic: In Taihe sixteen Rui won a Julu founding dukedom by citing his father's role with He's in enthroning Gaozong.

literal: Your servant at the time was in grass-soil mourning and could not reach the precedent.
idiomatic: Huai was in mourning and could not claim then.

literal: By the twentieth year your servant was removed as Governor of Yongzhou.
idiomatic: In year twenty he became governor of Yongzhou.

literal: On the eve of departure paying farewell, he faced the late emperor and memorialized his late father's old merit.
idiomatic: Leaving for Yong, he reminded the late emperor of his father's service.

literal: At the time he received an edict: only go to what you oversee; soon there will be separate judgment.
idiomatic: An edict told him to take the post; reward would follow.

literal: By the twenty-first year the imperial carriage visited Yong; your servant again stated it.
idiomatic: In year twenty-one, when the emperor visited Yong, he spoke again.

literal: At the time he received an edict: on recall he would be awarded.
idiomatic: He was told he would be enfeoffed on recall.

literal: From the imperial carriage's peaceful departure it was thus not stated.
idiomatic: After the emperor's death he could not press it.

literal: I reflect on your servant's late father—far then he received and established Gaozong; the precious succession did not fall;
idiomatic: His father had far back saved the succession when Gaozong was made emperor;

literal: near then he offered strength to Xianzu; the sacred vessel had a return.
idiomatic: near at hand he secured Xianzu's abdication to Gaozu.

literal: Merit like this is a matter surpassing the age.
idiomatic: Such merit outshone his generation.

literal: Li by his father's merit obtained reward of mountains and rivers;
idiomatic: Li won mountains-and-rivers reward for his father's deed;

literal: your servant has family merit yet does not touch the grant of thatch and soil.
idiomatic: Huai's house had equal merit yet no fief.

literal: Gain and denial hang apart—I ask to let judgment fall.
idiomatic: The disparity was unjust—he asked the throne to decide.

literal: " The edict said: "The old veteran minister of long standing—as the clouds report, inquiring of the historiographers it is quite also spoken thus."
idiomatic: The edict said the histories confirmed his plea.

literal: He may be enfeoffed according to appointment as Duke of Beifengyi commandery, state-founder, fief of nine hundred households."
idiomatic: He was made founding duke of Beifengyi with nine hundred households.

literal: He was again edicted Bearer of the Staff, added Palace Attendant and Mobile Headquarters, touring the northern frontier six garrisons and the three provinces Heng, Bei, and Shuo, relieving the poor and needy, also gathering folk songs, evaluating hall and precinct performance, the gains and losses of affairs—decide first then report.
idiomatic: He was sent with a staff as mobile headquarters to tour six northern garrisons and three provinces, aid the poor, hear folk songs, and judge officials.

literal: From the capital's move to Luoyang the northern frontier was far; moreover successive years of drought and dearth—the hundred surnames were distressed and worn.
idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang the north starved through drought after drought.

literal: Huai received the mandate to guide and comfort; preserving and cherishing had method; convenient transport and transfer—having and not having mutually aided.
idiomatic: Huai fed the frontier wisely and kept supplies moving.

literal: At the time the empress's father Yu Jin's power tilted court and countryside; Jin's elder brother's son Zuo had with Huai an old marriage; at the time he was Garrison Commander of Woye and quite had accepting and taking.
idiomatic: Empress Yu Jin's kin ruled the court; his nephew Zuo, Huai's in-law and Woye commander, took bribes.

literal: About to enter the garrison, Zuo met him on the road to the left in the suburbs; Huai did not communicate with him and immediately impeached Zuo and removed him from office.
idiomatic: Zuo met him outside town; Huai ignored him and impeached him from office.

literal: The Garrison Commander of Huaishuo Yuan Nixu had with Huai an old youth acquaintance and also was greedy and defiled in disarray.
idiomatic: Huaishuo commander Yuan Nixu, an old friend, was likewise corrupt.

literal: He set out wine and invited Huai, saying: "Whether life is long or short is by your mouth—how can you not mutually grant leniency?"
idiomatic: Nixu wined him and said, "My life is in your mouth—won't you spare me?"

literal: " Huai said: "Today's gathering is Yuan Huai drinking wine with an old friend—it is not a place for judging cases."
idiomatic: Huai said, "Tonight I drink with a friend—not a court of justice."
